articles.headline: Hong Kong Claims First Gold of Asian Para Games as Boccia Star Vivian Lau Triumphs in Nagoya
articles.summary_html:
Hong Kong secured the first gold medal of its campaign at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Nagoya on Wednesday, after boccia player Vivian Lau Wai-yan defeated her own compatriota fellow citizen from the same country or territory, here used of a teammate from the same delegation同胞（此處指同一代表隊的隊友） Cheung Yuen in an all-Hong Kong final. Bocciaa Paralympic precision ball sport in which players release soft balls toward a target, designed for athletes with severe impairments affecting motor control硬地滾球（殘奧會的一項講求準繩度的球類運動） is a precision sport designed for athletes with severe impairments affecting motor control, in which competitors roll or release soft leather balls toward a target ball from a fixed position on court. The sport operates under a classification systema framework that groups para-athletes into categories based on the type and severity of their impairment, so that competitors face others with comparable abilities殘疾分級制度 that groups players by the degree of physical impairment, ensuring that athletes with comparable support needs compete against one another rather than against the field as a whole.

The gold formed part of a strong day for the Hong Kong delegation, which added four silver and four bronze medals across several disciplines, lifting the city's overall medal tallythe running total of medals won by a team or country during a multi-sport event獎牌總數 at the Games to 21 — one gold, eight silver and twelve bronze — and placing Hong Kong 17th in the medal standingsthe ranking of countries or teams according to the number and type of medals they have won獎牌榜排名. The Games, running from 18 to 24 October across venues in Aichi and Nagoya, mark the fifth edition of the regional competition, held three years after Hong Kong's elite training squada specially selected group of top-performing athletes who train together at the highest competitive level精英訓練隊 returned from the 2023 Hangzhou Games with a then-record 47 medals.

Local sports officials have pointed to Wednesday's results as evidence that sustained parasports fundingfinancial support, usually from government or sports bodies, dedicated to training and competition for athletes with disabilities殘疾人士體育資助 and improved training facilities are beginning to pay off, with Hong Kong's para-athletes increasingly rivalling their able-bodied counterparts for public attention. Advocates for disability sport argue that each podium appearancean occasion on which an athlete finishes among the top three and is honoured on the winners' platform登上頒獎台 helps normalise the presence of athletes with impairments in mainstream sporting narratives, rather than confining their achievements to a separate, lower-profile category. With three days of competition remaining, officials have not ruled out further medals from a squad many regard as deeper and more competitive than in previous editions.
articles.summary_zh_html:
香港代表團周三在名古屋舉行的2026年亞洲殘疾人運動會中,贏得今屆賽事首金——硬地滾球選手劉慧茵在全港內部對決的決賽中,擊敗同為代表隊的同胞隊友Cheung Yuen。硬地滾球是專為肢體活動能力嚴重受限的運動員而設的講求準繩度的運動項目,參賽者須從場上固定位置,將軟身皮球擲向或滾向目標球。該項運動設有殘疾分級制度,按運動員肢體損傷的嚴重程度分組,確保支援需要相若的選手彼此對壘,而非與所有選手一概比較。

這面金牌是香港代表團表現出色的一天的縮影——當日港隊在多個項目中再添四銀四銅,令代表團在今屆運動會的獎牌總數增至21面(一金、八銀、十二銅),在獎牌榜排名中位列第十七。本屆賽事為期自10月18日至24日,在愛知及名古屋多個場館舉行,是這項地區性賽事的第五屆,距離港隊精英訓練隊在2023年杭州亞殘運創下當時破紀錄的47面獎牌,僅三年之隔。

本地體育官員指,周三的成績證明持續的殘疾人士體育資助及訓練設施的改善,正逐漸見到成效,香港殘疾運動員在公眾關注度上,正日益追上健全運動員。殘疾體育的支持者認為,每一次登上頒獎台的機會,都有助令傷殘運動員的身影,更自然地融入主流體育敘事之中,而非被局限於另一個較少受關注的類別。隨着賽事尚餘三日,官員未排除港隊這支普遍被視為陣容更深厚、競爭力更強的隊伍,能再添獎牌。

articles.headline: Star Ferry Fares to Rise Again as Executive Council Approves Smaller Increase Than Sought
articles.summary_html:
Hong Kong's Executive Councilthe body of senior officials that advises Hong Kong's Chief Executive and approves major government decisions, including regulated fare changes行政會議 approved a new round of fare increases for the Star Ferry on Wednesday, meaning passengers on the operator's two franchised routesferry or bus routes operated under an exclusive government licence, which also regulates the fares charged專營航線 will pay up to HK$1 more per journey on weekdays and up to HK$1.80 more on weekends and public holidays from 25 January next year. Under the approved schedule, weekday single-trip fares will rise by 60 cents to HK$1, capping the adult upper-deck fare at HK$6, while weekend and holiday fares will increase by HK$1 to HK$1.80, bringing the top fare to HK$8.30. The price of a monthly ticket will remain unchanged at HK$190.

The approved rise is noticeably smaller than what the ferry operator had originally sought in its fare increase applicationa formal request submitted by a transport operator asking the government to approve higher fares加價申請, which proposed increases of between 80 cents and HK$2 per trip, equivalent to an average rise of about 30 percent on both the Central–Tsim Sha Tsui and Wan Chai–Tsim Sha Tsui crossings. Officials said the government had moderated the increasereduced a proposed change to a smaller, less severe version before approving it調低加幅 after weighing the ferry's financial difficulties against concerns, raised repeatedly by lawmakers, that ordinary commuters should not bear the full cost of keeping a century-old service afloat. The revised fare schedule must still pass through negative vettinga legislative procedure in which a regulation automatically takes effect unless lawmakers vote to block it within a set period先訂立後審議程序 at the Legislative Council next Wednesday before it can take effect.

The Transport and Logistics Bureau said the adjustment was necessary because the Star Ferry recorded operating lossesthe amount by which a company's running costs exceed its income from normal business activities經營虧損 exceeding HK$100 million between 2018 and 2023, and has since relied on debt financingraising money by borrowing, such as through loans, rather than through revenue or investment債務融資 simply to maintain its franchised service. The last fare increase, approved in January 2023, raised prices by more than 50 percent, yet the operator argues that rising costs and falling patronage since the pandemic have continued to erode its finances. Commuter groups have urged the government to explore alternative subsidies rather than repeatedly passing costs onto fare-paying passengers.
articles.summary_zh_html:
香港行政會議周三批准天星小輪新一輪加價,意味渡輪兩條專營航線的乘客,由明年1月25日起,平日每程最多加價1元,假日及周末每程最多加價1.8元。根據獲批的新收費表,平日單程票價將上調6角至1元,成人上層票價上限為6元;周末及公眾假期票價則上調1元至1.8元,最高票價為8.3元。月票價格維持不變,仍為190元。

獲批的加幅,明顯低於渡輪公司原先在加價申請中提出的幅度——該申請要求兩條航線(中環至尖沙咀,以及灣仔至尖沙咀)每程加價8角至2元,平均加幅約30%。官員表示,政府在衡量渡輪公司的財政困難,與議員多次提出、不應由普通乘客全數承擔維持這項逾百年歷史服務所需開支的訴求後,調低加幅。修訂後的收費表仍須於下周三提交立法會,經先訂立後審議程序,方可正式生效。

運輸及物流局表示,有必要調整收費,因天星小輪在2018年至2023年間錄得超過1億元的經營虧損,其後僅靠債務融資維持其專營服務運作。上一次加價於2023年1月批准,加幅超過五成,但渡輪公司指,疫情後成本上升及客流下跌,持續侵蝕其財政狀況。多個關注團體促請政府研究其他資助方案,而非一再將成本轉嫁予付費乘客。

articles.headline: Property Agent Tells Abby Choi Murder Trial Ex-Father-in-Law Pocketed HK$6.97 Million Flat Rebate
articles.summary_html:
An estate agenta licensed professional who arranges and negotiates property sales on behalf of buyers, sellers or developers地產代理 told the High Court on Wednesday that Abby Choi's former father-in-law, Kwong Kau, personally asked for and received a cash rebatea sum of money paid back to a buyer after a purchase, often deducted from a commission or the sale price現金回贈 of roughly HK$6.97 million after the purchase of a Kadoorie Hill flat funded by the slain socialite. Marco Wong Tak-sing, giving evidence on the 20th day of the murder trial, said his agency earned about HK$8.18 million in sales commissiona fee, usually a percentage of the sale price, paid to an agent for arranging a transaction銷售佣金 from the flat's developer, and that most of that sum was then passed back to Kwong, the flat's registered ownerthe person or entity whose name legally appears on a property's title documents登記業主, at his own request.

Wong told the court that a deposit chequea cheque used to pay the initial, partial payment required to secure a property purchase訂金支票 worth HK$3.74 million had been drawn directly on Choi's own bank account, and that Kwong explained at the time that his daughter-in-law had provided the funds. Under cross-examinationthe questioning of a witness by the opposing side in a trial, used to test or challenge their evidence盤問, Wong was pressed on why the buyer's correspondence address listed on the tender documentthe formal paperwork submitted when bidding to purchase a property through a sealed-bid process投標文件 was his own agency's address rather than Kwong's, and replied that the arrangement was meant to stop the purchaser from contacting the developer directly — a point Kwong is said to have agreed to at the time.

The testimony adds financial detail to the prosecution's broader case, which alleges that Kwong Kau held the flat only in a beneficial ownershipthe right to enjoy the benefits of an asset even though it is legally registered in someone else's name實益擁有權 arrangement on Choi's behalf, and that his resentment over her eventual decision to sell it helped drive the killing. Kwong, 68, is on trial alongside his sons Alex and Anthony Kwong, all of whom deny murdering the 28-year-old influencer in 2023; the two sons have separately pleaded guilty to preventing her lawful burial, a charge their father continues to contest.
articles.summary_zh_html:
一名地產代理周三在高等法院作證指,名模Abby Choi的前家翁鄺球,在以Choi出資購入嘉道理山一個單位後,曾親自要求並取得約697萬元的現金回贈。黃德誠(譯名)在謀殺審訊第20日作供時表示,其代理行就該單位的買賣,從發展商處收取約818萬元銷售佣金,其中大部分款項隨後按鄺球本人的要求,回贈予身為單位登記業主的他。

黃又向法庭表示,一張金額374萬元的訂金支票,直接從Choi本人的銀行帳戶支取,鄺球當時解釋,款項是由其媳婦提供。在盤問環節中,黃被追問為何投標文件上所列的買家聯絡地址,是其代理行的地址,而非鄺球本人的地址,他回應指,此安排是為免買家直接聯絡發展商——而鄺球當時據稱亦同意此做法。

今次證供,為控方更廣泛的案情增添財務細節——控方指,鄺球僅以實益擁有權的安排,代表Choi持有該單位,而他對Choi最終決定出售單位心存不滿,正是促使這宗謀殺案發生的原因之一。68歲的鄺球,與其兩名兒子Alex Kwong及Anthony Kwong一同受審,三人均否認於2023年謀殺這名28歲網絡紅人;兩名兒子已就妨礙合法埋葬罪另行認罪,惟其父則繼續否認該項控罪。

articles.headline: Parents of Girl, 5, Who Died After Stitching Procedure Sue Hospital Authority for Negligence
articles.summary_html:
The parents of a girl who died after a medical procedure at a public hospital have filed a civil suita legal case brought by one private party against another, or a public body, seeking compensation rather than criminal punishment民事訴訟 against the Hospital Authority, alleging negligence that led to their daughter's death nearly a year after the original incident. According to a writ of summonsthe formal document that officially starts a civil lawsuit in court傳訊令狀 filed at the District Courta Hong Kong court that handles civil claims above a certain value and some criminal cases, ranking below the High Court區域法院 last Thursday, Lai Sum-yuet, then aged four, was taken to Yan Chai Hospital in Tsuen Wan in May 2024 to have a head wound from a fall treated, a routine suturing procedurea medical procedure in which stitches are used to close a wound縫合程序 expected to take only a few minutes.

The writ states that once the brief procedure was completed, a nurse found that the child had lost consciousness and had no pulse, and that medical staff spent 18 minutes performing resuscitation before restoring her heartbeat following a cardiac arresta sudden stop in effective heart function, cutting off blood flow to the body心臟停頓. Lai never fully recovered and died in February this year, at the age of five. Her family has previously said they witnessed hospital staff pressing the girl's head firmly against a pillow during the procedure, a claim at the centre of separate criminal proceedings in which two medical staff members have been charged with the ill-treatment or neglect of a childa criminal offence covering wilful cruelty or culpable failure to care for a child in one's charge對兒童虐待或忽略罪.

The Hospital Authority has apologised for the family's loss but has maintained that staff followed established protocolsthe official, standard procedures that staff are trained and expected to follow既定程序 throughout the procedure, a position the lawsuit now directly challenges. The case has also been referred to the Coroner's Courta court that formally investigates the cause and circumstances of an unexplained or unnatural death死因裁判法庭 for a separate inquest into the circumstances of the child's death, running alongside both the criminal case and the newly filed civil claim. The writ does not specify the amount of damages being sought, but it marks the family's latest step in a long pursuit of accountability for what they describe as an entirely preventable tragedy.
articles.summary_zh_html:
一名女童在公立醫院接受醫療程序後死亡,其父母已就院方疏忽,向醫院管理局提出民事訴訟,事件發生近一年後終告上法庭。根據上周四提交的傳訊令狀,案件已於區域法院展開法律程序。令狀指,黎心悅(譯名)在2024年5月,當時年僅四歲,因跌傷頭部被送往荃灣仁濟醫院,接受一項原本預計僅需數分鐘的常規縫合程序。

令狀指出,該簡短程序完成後,護士發現女童已失去知覺並無脈搏,醫護人員經過18分鐘的搶救,方令她在一次心臟停頓後恢復心跳。黎心悅自此未能完全康復,並於今年2月,年僅五歲時離世。其家人早前表示,曾目擊院方職員在進行程序期間,用力將女童的頭按向枕頭,此說法正是另一宗刑事案件的爭議核心——兩名醫護人員已被控對兒童虐待或忽略罪。

醫院管理局已就該家庭的喪女之痛致歉,但一直堅稱職員在整個程序中均遵從既定程序,而今次民事訴訟,正正直接挑戰這一說法。案件亦已轉交死因裁判法庭另行展開死因調查,與刑事案件及今次新提出的民事索償同步進行。令狀並未指明索償金額,但事件標誌着這家庭在追究一場他們形容為完全可以避免的悲劇責任路上,邁出的最新一步。
articles.image_scene: The quiet exterior of a Hong Kong public hospital in Tsuen Wan on an overcast afternoon, its entrance canopy and ambulance bay empty of people; a single potted plant and an informational signboard blank of text near the doorway, a small bouquet of flowers left respectfully on a nearby bench, no people, text or logos visible.

trends.headline: 😡📱 Viral 'Family Discipline' Alley Beating Clip Ignites Vigilante Justice Debate
trends.summary_html:
A short video showing a teenager being knocked to the ground and repeatedly slapped in a Hong Kong alley, while three bystanders stood by and did nothing, has become one of the most argued-over clips on local social media this week. The man seen attacking the teenager wore a cap and struck him both with an open hand and on the head, all while shouting at him; the person who uploaded the footage gave no account of when or where it happened, captioning it only as ‘time for family discipline’ — language that immediately split opinion between viewers who assumed it showed a parent disciplining a wayward child and those who saw nothing but an unprovoked assault dressed up in more acceptable-sounding words.

The ambiguity is precisely what has kept the clip circulating. Commenters have pressed the uploader to explain who the attacker was and whether anyone had reported the incident to police, while others have pointed out that filming and sharing an assault, rather than intervening or calling for help, risks turning real violence into entertainment. With neither the people involved nor the exact circumstances ever confirmed, the clip has become less a single verified incident than a mirror for whatever assumptions viewers already hold about discipline, masculinity and family authority in Hong Kong.
trends.summary_zh_html:
一段片段顯示,一名少年在香港一條後巷內被推倒在地並遭多次掌摑,三名途人在場卻無人阻止,片段近日在本地社交媒體上引起熾熱爭論。片中一名戴着帽子的男子衝向少年,用手掌及拳頭擊打其頭部,同時高聲喝罵;上載片段者並未透露事發的時間或地點,僅以「教仔」(家庭教訓)作為描述——這種說法,立即令網民意見兩極:有人假設片中情景只是家長教訓頑劣子女,亦有人則認為,這純粹是一宗以較「順耳」字眼包裝的無故襲擊事件。

正是這種模糊性,令片段持續被轉發。有網民追問上載者,片中施襲者的身份,以及事件有否已經報警;另有網民則指出,目擊襲擊卻只顧拍片上載、而非上前阻止或求助,恐會令真實的暴力行為淪為娛樂內容。由於片中人物身份及事發經過始終未獲證實,這段片段與其說是一宗經核實的單一事件,倒更似一塊鏡子,映照出香港社會對「教養」、「男子氣概」與「家長權威」各自既有的假設與想像。

causes.label: Filming an assault instead of stopping it
causes.text: Three onlookers watched the beating unfold yet none intervened or called for help; the footage exists only because someone chose to film rather than act. A Paper 2 essay could ask whether smartphones have quietly replaced a moral duty to help a stranger with a reflex to document them instead, and what that substitution costs a community.

causes.label: 'Family discipline' as a euphemism that reframes violence
causes.text: Calling the beating 'family discipline' let the uploader present unverified, uncontextualised violence as something socially acceptable, without ever confirming who the people involved were. Students could explore how a single caption can steer thousands of viewers toward forgiving, or even endorsing, an act they would otherwise condemn, and why audiences rarely demand evidence before reacting.

causes.label: Calling it discipline doesn't exempt it from assault law
causes.text: However the clip was captioned, repeatedly striking a minor's head in public meets the legal threshold for assault, regardless of any claimed disciplinary motive. An essay could examine why online audiences debated the footage for days while seemingly few considered reporting it, and what that says about public reliance on formal authorities.

causes.label: Counter-argument: online outrage can misfire and punish the wrong person
causes.text: Without confirmed identities, a wave of comments demanding the attacker be named risks misdirecting anger at an innocent bystander wrongly assumed to be him, a pattern seen in past Hong Kong cases of mistaken online identification. A sharper essay might argue that collective fury, however well-intentioned, is a poor substitute for a verified police investigation and due process.
